heroHeadline: ICE Agents Pose as Utility Workers in Tucson; Sen. Kim Pepper-Sprayed at Delaney Hall; Senate Reconvenes With $71.7B Vote Imminent
heroSubtitle: On May 28, 2026, ICE agents in Tucson, Arizona posed as Tucson Electric Power workers to attempt the arrest of a long-term Honduran resident — a neighbor spotted a badge and alerted the target before the arrest could be made, while Tucson Electric Power publicly objected to the impersonation. The Delaney Hall crisis deepened on May 27 when Sen. Andy Kim (D-NJ) reported being pepper-sprayed by federal agents during a congressional oversight visit; Gov. Mikie Sherrill's delegation was also blocked from entering; an ICE agent was caught on video pushing a protester under a moving tractor-trailer; and President Trump dismissed demonstrators as 'paid.' Most detainees ended their hunger strike as of May 27–28 but the labor strike continued. The Senate reconvened May 28 following the Memorial Day recess with a floor vote on the $71.7 billion ICE and CBP reconciliation package — the largest single-year immigration enforcement investment in U.S. history — now expected the week of June 1, after Trump's original June 1 signing deadline was effectively missed.
